kitDescription: Guillotine: Winter Slayer is a Water-element AR attacker who builds her own power over the course of a fight. Her normal attacks earn EXP (one EXP per 3 core hits, or per 6 non-core hits), and each EXP stack permanently raises her own ATK by 1.81% up to 100 stacks; every 10 EXP she also gains a Hero Level, capped at Level 11, and each level-up instantly tops up part of her magazine and heals her a little. Because the EXP pool itself caps at 100, exactly ten level-ups happen in a fight and then the rewards stop. Every Hero Level she gains makes her stronger for the whole Water side of the team: all Water Code allies (herself included) get Elemental Advantage Attack Damage and a flat ATK boost drawn from her own ATK, both scaling with her current Hero Level, and from Level 2 on she keeps an extra personal +7.46% Elemental Advantage Attack Damage. Her Burst III gives all Water Code allies +10.14% Attack Damage and +18.75% Elemental Advantage Attack Damage for 10 seconds, and plants a 10-second damage-over-time on the biggest enemy that ticks once a second for 20.87% of her final ATK multiplied by her Hero Level — so the same burst hits far harder late in a fight than at the start.

redAssertions: T10 'EXP accrues on BOTH the 6-non-core path and the 3-core path': the driver still ships only a hitCount:3 block, no hitCount:6 and no requiresCore. CLASSIFIED DOCUMENTED_GAP — the engine resolves core as a per-shot rate (coreExposure × ACR) folded into the Major bucket, not as discrete core/non-core hit events, so a hitCount trigger cannot be routed to exactly one branch; authoring both would double-feed the counter. Three independent agents hit the same wall and all flagged rather than silently picked. ⚑2 carries the blend recipe.

T12 '7.46% line is level-gated (not a t=0 passive)': the behavioural half (self-only, helm excluded, permanent) PASSES; only the structural `trigger.kind !== 'passive' || resourceGate != null` check fails. CLASSIFIED DOCUMENTED_GAP — quantified at ~3s of 180s on one buff ≈ 0.1% of carry, named in note + caveats.
RESOLVED THIS PASS: T9 'Hero Level scaling is live' flipped GREEN — the new resources[heroLevel]{initial 1, max 11} pool satisfies the blind's declared-pool branch. Blind tally moved 13/3/2 → 14/2/2.

skill1.kitLine: every time EXP stacks 10 … max Lv 11
skill1.driverSaid: resources[{heroLevel, initial 1, min 1, max 11}]; hitCount:30 increment block {kind:'resource', heroLevel, delta:1} ordered AFTER the two gated reward blocks; resourceGate{heroLevel, max 10} on both rewards.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 specified exactly this encoding (pool initial 1 / max 11 + resourceGate max 10) with the warning 'without that gate the hitCount trigger would keep paying rewards forever past Level 11'; S2b pre-registered 'rewards stop firing at cap'. The shipped fix is now byte-equivalent to the blind's independent derivation.
skill1.formulaCheck: Kit arithmetic self-closes: S2 caps EXP at 100, S1 levels per 10 EXP → 100/10 = 10 level-ups → Level 1→11 = the stated cap. Block-order semantics give the gated rewards the PRE-increment value, so they admit heroLevel ∈ {1..10} = exactly 10 firings, then the pool reaches 11 and the gate closes. Corroborated independently of the code path by the engine DBG resource log: 10 real increases (1→2 @2.62s … 10→11 @27.97s), clamped '11+1 → 11' thereafter.
skill1.explanation: The prior REAL-GOTCHA is closed at the mechanism level, not papered over. The cap is now the kit's own arithmetic expressed in the engine's own primitive, and the DBG count (10, terminating at 27.97s) is an independent confirmation of the array-order reasoning rather than a restatement of it. The unsupported 'rewards KEEP TRIGGERING at max level (review-confirmed)' note claim is retracted.

skill1.driverSaid: instantReload fraction 0.1026, hitCount:30, self, resourceGate{heroLevel max 10}.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 same effect + fraction + gate; S2b FAITHFUL and load-bearing with 'stops firing once Level 11 is reached'.
skill1.formulaCheck: Reload economy is shot economy is damage. Carry moved 1881 → 1846 shots (−35) and 269.7M → 266.2M damage on the fix. Cross-check: at ~0.82 shots per firing (the pre-fix G2 measurement of ~46 shots across ~56 firings), removing 46 firings predicts ≈ −38 shots — observed −35, consistent. Note the damage delta is −1.30%, not the −1.7% the driver's self-report states; that is marginally BELOW my prior 1.5–1.7% band, which is expected since the shots removed are spread outside Full-Burst windows. Direction and order of magnitude both check out; no contradiction, only a slightly overstated self-report number.
skill1.explanation: Fraction, routing, target and now CADENCE are all faithful. The block fires 10× at the prose-implied level-up rate, and the shot-count delta proves the gate is live rather than a decorative field.

skill1.driverSaid: heal event block (no value), self, hitCount:30, resourceGate{heroLevel max 10}; G3 asserts the gate is present and that the block moves zero damage in this comp.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical event-only heal under the same gate; S2b flagged it as the on-recovery inertness pin.
skill1.formulaCheck: Damage-inert here (no HP pool, no recovery-consumer in the control comp) — `base.totals` equals `noHeal.totals` exactly. The omitted 2.44% magnitude is an engine-shape consequence (no HP pool exists to apply it to) and is recorded in the note, not hidden; the observable the engine does carry — the recovery PROC on a cross-unit channel — now fires the kit-permitted 10 times instead of ~56.
skill1.explanation: Represented (hard rule 2 satisfied), correctly inert on this board, and now correctly counted for any future comp that consumes ally-recovery events.

skill1.kitLine: Elem Adv Atk Dmg ▲1.16% * Hero Level
skill1.driverSaid: passive alliesOfElement Water, elemAdvantageDamagePct 12.76 = 1.16 × 11, permanent; ramp collapsed to the Level-11 steady state under ⚑3 with a refit recipe.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 encoded perResource{heroLevel, mult 1.16} off a live pool but flagged its own unresolved risk that perResource may not resolve for ally targets; S2b called the collapse the nearest-wrong and asked for a ramp.
skill1.formulaCheck: elemAdvantageDamagePct is the Element bucket (superior-element term), live only under advantage; the control boss is Fire so it is genuinely live. Magnitude is the kit's own per-level value × the kit's own cap — no prose number contradicted (contract F). The DBG log now DATES the ramp precisely: Level 11 at 27.97s, so ~15.5% of the 180s fight is held above the true value. Unchanged from the prior ruling except that the ramp's endpoint is now measured rather than estimated.
skill1.explanation: Stat key, scope (two-sided: target set exactly {gws, helm}, Fire crown byte-identical under the counterfactual) and permanence faithful; the trajectory approximation is a recorded ⚑ with estimate + recipe. Ruled FAITHFUL-as-calibrated in the prior packet and nothing in the fix disturbs it.

skill1.kitLine: ATK ▲0.91% of skill user's ATK * Level
skill1.blindSaid: S6 perResource{heroLevel, mult 0.91} on casterAtkPct — same stat, same scope, same excludeSelf:false judgment.
skill1.formulaCheck: Correct basis: casterAtkPct resolves at application to a FLAT add of the caster's static ATK × pct, OUTSIDE each recipient's (1+ΣATK%) sum — the S2b nearest-wrong (atkPct, i.e. target-own-ATK scaled) is avoided. The S5 blind's value-grouping assertion finds a casterAtkPct group whose target set is exactly {gws, helm} and passes.

The overstated premise I flagged last pass is retired — the note now states the exposure-vs-realised-fraction distinction correctly and names the consequence (Level 11 arrives LATER than modeled, lengthening the ⚑3 over-credit window).

RESIDUAL, non-blocking: the TEST file header still carries the old prose — 'scope-lock = 100% core exposure, so the 6-non-core-hit branch never fires' — and separately still asserts 'the first burst lands at 40s CD, so level 11 is guaranteed by then', which the note itself now contradicts (first burst ~5s on an early B1→B2→B3 chain, Level 11 at 27.97s). The shipped file is correct (initial 1, min 1) and the DBG log confirms 10 increments 1→11, so this is a test-completeness hole, not a live defect. The behavioural counterfactual (gwsNoGate) discriminates gate-present from gate-absent but not gate-at-10 from gate-at-9-or-11.

verdictRationale: The REAL-GOTCHA is fixed faithfully and at the mechanism level. The driver implemented the exact encoding both blind agents independently specified — resources[heroLevel]{initial 1, min 1, max 11}, an increment on the hitCount:30 level-up, and resourceGate{heroLevel, max 10} on BOTH reward blocks — so the kit's own self-closing arithmetic (100 EXP ÷ 10 per level = 10 level-ups = Level 1→11) is now expressed in the engine's own primitive rather than asserted in prose. Three independent lines of evidence agree that the cap is live and lands on exactly 10: the block-order argument (gated rewards read the pre-increment value, admitting heroLevel ∈ {1..10}), the engine DBG resource log (10 increases, 1→2 @2.62s … 10→11 @27.97s, clamped thereafter), and the carry movement (1881→1846 shots), which matches the ~38-shot loss predicted from the pre-fix G2 measurement of ~46 shots across ~56 firings. One self-report correction, immaterial to the verdict: the damage delta is −1.30% (269.7M→266.2M), marginally under the 1.5–1.7% band I predicted, not the −1.7% the driver states — expected, since the removed shots fall largely outside Full-Burst windows. On discrimination I asked for an event count and accept the substitute: the engine emits no countable reload or heal event (instantReload adjusts ammo inline, heal calls fireRecovery internally), so 'exactly 10' is not directly assertable, and the driver instead pins the cap structurally (pool max 11 + two gates at max 10 + an increment block) and discriminates it behaviourally against the named nearest-wrong model — the gwsNoGate counterfactual strips both gates and the test requires shipped shots AND damage to be strictly less. That test throws 'fixture is stale' under the pre-fix uncapped override and passes under the fix, which is precisely the fail-under-nearest-wrong property the contract demands; discriminationOk flips to true. Both note corrections landed: the unsupported 'review-confirmed keep triggering at max level' claim is retracted with the S7 finding cited, and the skill2 prose now states the exposure × ACR distinction and its consequence (Level 11 arrives later than modeled, lengthening the ⚑3 window). All twelve kit lines are now FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP → 1.0. The blind suite improved to 14/2/2 with T9 flipping green off the new pool; the two remaining reds are the ones I already ruled — T10 (engine cannot partition core from non-core per hit; three agents converged on the same wall and all flagged) and T12 (structural-only, behavioural half green, now measured at 2.62s of 180s ≈ 0.07% of carry). Two low findings remain, neither blocking and neither an encoding defect on the shipped model: the test-file header still carries the two sentences the note just corrected (including 'the first burst lands at 40s CD', which the DBG log now falsifies outright), and G2 pins pool.max but not pool.initial, so an off-by-one starting value would pass both suites. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check, ranked: (1) the first burst's DoT — the fix's own DBG trajectory tightens this rather than resolving it, since a ~5s first cast is at roughly Level 2–3, making that cast's ten ticks a ~4× over-credit, not the ~2–3× I estimated before; a solo footage read should settle it first. (2) Whether the ⚑1 normal-fire cadence (pullsPerSec 12 / reloadFrames 81, measured ~26% hot) is silently absorbing part of the steady-state over-credit — a hot fire rate and an early-peaked ATK ramp compensate each other, both are unmeasured, and the level-up cadence now depends on the same shot rate. (3) That the resourceGate comparison is inclusive at max as the block-order argument assumes; the DBG count corroborates it here, but it is an engine-semantics premise worth one direct read if the primitive gets reused.
